notes: All five advertised tools reach only AWS-operated hosts: docs.aws.amazon.com / awsdocs-neuron.readthedocs-hosted.com for page fetches, proxy.search.docs.aws.com for search, api.contentrecs.docs.aws.com for recommendations.

`enforce_redirect_allowlist` (util.py:165-186) explicitly blocks the classic redirect-to-link-local/metadata escape that `follow_redirects=True` would otherwise permit, which is why the read tools get no SECRET label.

Residual, unlabeled risk: `recommend` does not validate its `url` argument at all (server_aws.py:696-699) — arbitrary agent text is placed in the `path` query parameter of the fixed AWS recommendations endpoint. Because the scheme/host prefix is a literal constant and a `?` already precedes the injected value, the destination host cannot be changed, so this is not treated as a SINK.

The neuron docs host is on the readthedocs-hosted.com platform, but the allowlist regex pins the exact `awsdocs-neuron` subdomain (server_utils.py:40), an AWS-published docs project, so it is not treated as attacker-controllable content.

read_documentation.rationale: `read_documentation` validates `url` against `supported_domains_regex` (`^https?://docs\.aws\.amazon\.com/` plus the neuron readthedocs regex) and requires a `.html` suffix (server_aws.py:184-193), then fetches via `_docs_client`, whose `enforce_redirect_allowlist` response hook re-checks every redirect `Location` against `COMMERCIAL_ALLOWED_DOMAIN_REGEXES` (server_utils.py:44-48, util.py:173-184). The host is therefore pinned to AWS-published public documentation: no file://, localhost or intranet reach (no SECRET), no attacker-chosen destination for the agent-supplied URL or `query_id` (no SINK), and the returned markdown comes from a first-party vendor docs site rather than a multi-writer/attacker-controllable source (no UNTRUSTED). No code execution.

read_sections.rationale: Same domain allowlist and `.html` check as `read_documentation` (server_aws.py:260-269); `read_sections_impl` only appends url-quoted `sections` parameters to the allow-listed URL and fetches with the redirect-revalidating client (server_utils.py:180-199). Content returned is public AWS documentation HTML converted to markdown, so no SECRET/UNTRUSTED/SINK reach.

recommend.rationale: `recommend` interpolates the caller-supplied `url_str` only into the query string of the hardcoded `RECOMMENDATIONS_API_URL` (`https://api.contentrecs.docs.aws.com/v1/recommendations?path=...`, server_aws.py:699), so the network destination cannot be chosen by the agent even though `url_str` itself is unvalidated — a fixed vendor endpoint is not a SINK. The response is parsed by `parse_recommendation_results` into AWS doc URLs/titles/abstracts (util.py:368-420), first-party public content; no local or credentialed data is read.

search_documentation.rationale: The request goes only to the hardcoded `SEARCH_API_URL` = `https://proxy.search.docs.aws.com/search` (server_aws.py:49, 490-499); `search_phrase`/`search_intent` are sent to that fixed vendor endpoint, which the rules say is not a SINK. Results are AWS-curated documentation titles, excerpts and URLs (server_aws.py:624-634), i.e. first-party public content, not attacker-writable, and nothing user-private is read.

search_table.rationale: `search_table` enforces the same `supported_domains_regex` allowlist and `.html` suffix (server_aws.py:365-374) and `search_table_impl` fetches the allow-listed doc URL with `quote`-escaped `query`/`section` params through `_docs_client` (server_utils.py:262-282). Output is parsed rows from the public AWS docs page; destination host is fixed to AWS docs, so no sink, secret data, or attacker-controlled content.

value_conditions.default: A Chrome-like UA string suffixed with ModelContextProtocol/<version> (AWS Documentation Server)
value_conditions.effect: Overrides the base User-Agent string sent with documentation fetches; does not change which hosts are reachable or any label.

Selects the fetch allowlist; the advertised commercial tools always pass the commercial allowlist, pinning fetches to docs.aws.amazon.com and awsdocs-neuron.readthedocs-hosted.com. The China entrypoint (server_aws_cn.py) exposes a different tool set (read_documentation, get_available_services) that is not advertised here.
